sources.verified_fact: The official release reports 6,000 child and family social-worker vacancies at 30 September 2025, a 14% vacancy rate and agency workers covering 74% of vacancies. Kensington and Chelsea and Westminster could not provide data after a November 2025 cyberattack affected their systems.
sources.quality_effect: Adds safeguarding-workforce capacity context while retaining FTE-versus-headcount, vacancy-definition, agency-cover, caseload, missing-authority and reporting-year guards; workforce capacity is not measured child harm or parcel risk.

sources.source: Fostering in England 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025
sources.verified_fact: The accredited release reports 42,190 fostering households and 69,825 approved mainstream fostering places at 31 March 2025. Around 60% of places were filled, 17% vacant and roughly one fifth unavailable.
sources.quality_effect: Adds placement-capacity context while separating households, carers, approved places, filled places, vacant places and unavailable places and retaining local-authority-versus-independent-agency and snapshot-date guards.

sources.source: Support in domestic abuse safe accommodation: 2024 to 2025
sources.authority: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.verified_fact: The management-information release reports 76,850 individuals supported in safe accommodation and 28,190 households unable to be supported between April 2024 and March 2025. Some questions are voluntary, people can receive multiple support types, and the data do not measure service quality or duration.
sources.quality_effect: Adds support-demand context with individual-versus-household, supported-versus-unable-to-support, voluntary-question, multiple-service and quality-duration guards; service use is not prevalence or local parcel safety.

sources.source: Statutory homelessness in England: October to December 2025
sources.authority: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.verified_fact: The accredited release reports 134,210 households in temporary accommodation at 31 December 2025, including 85,800 households with children and 176,130 dependent children. The household total fell 0.4% from the previous quarter but remained 5.0% above a year earlier.
sources.quality_effect: Adds housing-vulnerability context while retaining household-versus-person, duty-stage, stock-date, temporary-accommodation-type, out-of-area and policy-process guards; homelessness records are not crime incidence.

sources.source: Rough sleeping data framework, January to March 2026
sources.authority: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.verified_fact: The management-information release estimates 7,541 people sleeping rough over the month in March 2026 and 3,461 on a single night. It reports 3,045 long-term rough sleepers and explicitly distinguishes monthly flow from a point-in-time count.
sources.quality_effect: Adds acute-vulnerability context with management-information, estimate, monthly-flow, single-night, repeat-observation, outreach-coverage and local-practice guards; it is not accredited prevalence or parcel risk.

sources.verified_fact: The accredited release reports 5,600 active or suspended children's social-care providers at 31 March 2025, excluding local authorities and Cafcass. Ofsted later revised the dataset to add 16 previously omitted children's-home places and corrected one inspection-publication date.
sources.quality_effect: Adds provider-capacity and inspection context with provider-versus-place, active-versus-suspended, inspection-date, subtype, revision and regulatory-scope guards.

sources.source: Ownership of children's social care providers in England 2025
sources.verified_fact: The official-statistics-in-development release reports 81,770 children in care at 31 March 2025, with 40% in private provision. Ownership data link Ofsted records to Companies House information that is supplied by companies and is not verified by Companies House.
sources.quality_effect: Adds provider-concentration context while retaining child-versus-place, provider-versus-owner, ownership-chain, overseas-owner visibility, self-reported-company-data and development-statistics guards.

sources.source: Local authority inspection outcomes as at 31 March 2025
sources.verified_fact: The official release reports that 67% of England's 153 local authorities were good or outstanding at their most recent inspection as at 31 March 2025. The help-and-protection judgement was good or outstanding for 61%, and Ofsted warns that regional proportions can involve low numbers.
sources.quality_effect: Adds service-quality context while retaining latest-inspection-date, framework, judgement-area, inspection-cycle, regional-small-number and service-performance-versus-harm guards.

sources.source: Work-related fatal injuries in Great Britain: 2025/26
sources.verified_fact: HSE reports 126 workers and 104 members of the public killed in work-related accidents in 2025/26. The worker data are provisional under RIDDOR and are scheduled to be finalised in July 2027; HSE advises using rates when comparing over time.
sources.quality_effect: Adds occupational-safety context with worker-versus-public, RIDDOR-reportability, enforcing-authority, provisional-revision, industry-exposure and count-versus-rate guards.

sources.source: Annual report of health and safety on Britain's railways 2025 to 2026
sources.verified_fact: The regulator's 14 July 2026 report describes broadly stable overall outcomes but says risk management is not yet delivering the required control and assurance. Its assessment combines actual harm, modelled risk, inspections, investigations, near misses, asset performance and safety culture.
sources.quality_effect: Adds rail-system assurance context while separating actual harm, modelled risk, management maturity, inspection evidence and forthcoming statistical releases; a regulator assessment is not a parcel-level incident rate.

sources.verified_fact: AAIB reports 783 occurrence notifications in 2025, 12 investigations into fatal accidents involving 18 deaths, 198 final reports, 9 Safety Recommendations and 97 significant Safety Actions taken by industry in response to investigations.
sources.quality_effect: Adds aviation-investigation context while separating notification, classification, investigation, fatal accident, final report, recommendation and industry action; investigation workload is not an occurrence rate without exposure data.

sources.verified_fact: RAIB reports that 2025 activity resulted in 16 full investigations and 8 safety digests. It published 10 full investigation reports and 6 safety digests, with an average publication time of 11.7 months, and issued urgent safety advice during the year.
sources.quality_effect: Adds independent rail-investigation context while separating preliminary examination, full investigation, digest, report, urgent advice and publication delay; RAIB investigates for prevention and does not establish blame or liability.

sources.source: Road traffic estimates in Great Britain: 2025
sources.verified_fact: The official release estimates 262.4 billion car miles, 58.8 billion van miles and 16.3 billion lorry miles in Great Britain during 2025. England's Strategic Road Network carried 99.2 billion vehicle miles.
sources.quality_effect: Adds transport-exposure denominators while retaining estimated-versus-observed, vehicle-class, road-type, network, methodology and exposure-versus-collision guards; traffic volume is not safety performance by itself.

quality_guards: AREA_LEVEL_PROXY only; no parcel measurement claim.
Social-work workforce FTE, vacancies, agency cover and caseload are distinct measures, and two local-authority returns were unavailable.
Fostering households, carers and approved, filled, vacant or unavailable places must not be conflated.
Domestic-abuse safe-accommodation management information contains voluntary fields and does not measure service quality or duration.
Homelessness data count households and statutory duties; temporary accommodation is a stock at a specific date.
Rough-sleeping monthly flow and single-night estimates are management information and use different observation windows.
Children's social-care provider, place, inspection and ownership records have separate scopes and revision risks.
Local-authority inspection outcomes reflect each authority's latest inspection and regional percentages can involve small numbers.
HSE fatality figures for 2025/26 are provisional RIDDOR counts; rates are preferable for trend comparisons.
ORR regulatory assessment combines actual harm, modelled risk and assurance evidence rather than a single incident statistic.
AAIB and RAIB notifications, investigations, reports, recommendations, digests and actions are different operational units.
Road-traffic vehicle miles are exposure denominators and cannot be interpreted as safety outcomes without collision and casualty data.
